chapters.title: The Names on the Board
chapters.text: Irina Sokol found her name written neatly at the edge of the board. Anton Rask had left room beside it for a nickname, which Daria Vesnin erased before he could invent one. Lev Miren arrived carrying a headset and four mismatched cups. The board listed work, names and spaces where somebody would eventually have to answer a question. Irina had expected to be measured against a machine. Instead Daria asked how she wanted a mistake recorded when she was not in the room to explain it. Anton said he preferred not to make any. They laughed, and Irina understood that the joke was a small invitation to decide how seriously they would take one another.

options.label: Put my name beside an unfinished answer.
options.reply: Daria gives Irina a line others may question, while Anton wonders whether being visible will make every hesitation harder.

options.label: Let the four of us settle questions privately.
options.reply: Lev draws the chairs closer, making a welcoming first room whose unspoken rules newcomers will have to learn later.

chapters.title: A Mark That Looked Complete
chapters.text: The classroom rig would complete its sequence only if Anton held a worn contact in place. He did it with the easy satisfaction of somebody helping before being asked. Irina watched the indicator settle and reached for the completion mark. Daria put a second pencil beside hers. The exercise had succeeded, she agreed; the rig had not become reliable because a willing person had lent it a hand. Lev wanted to finish before the next group arrived. Anton wanted his useful trick to remain a favor rather than become the reason everyone waited for him. The square on the board was large enough for a clear mark, but not for the whole explanation.

options.label: Write the extra help into the completion note.
options.reply: The next instructor receives an honest account of what made the exercise succeed, and Anton helps explain what the record should not leave out.

options.label: Keep the qualification within the crew.
options.reply: They work through the difficult step in private, leaving a reassuringly clean account for the next group.

condition_variants.trigger: has_capitulated = no has_war = no ac_sq_air_capable = yes
condition_variants.text: Snow streamed across the edge of Irina's windscreen during the return exercise. Anton reached the next call before she did, then quietly corrected a distance he had taken from the wrong line. Lev asked both pilots to repeat it. The proper answer cost them an extra circuit and the fuel they had hoped to save. Back inside, Anton put his gloves on the board's ledge as though that could keep the discussion ordinary. He had helped her through the difficult part; he had also needed her to notice his error. Daria wanted the next pair to understand which check had made the return safe. Irina could put the qualification beside both names, or practice it with Anton first and preserve the clean account. Outside, the next crew was clearing snow from its equipment.

chapters.title: Two Telephones
chapters.text: Lev held two callers on separate lines. One wanted a training appointment moved; the other was trying to find a person whose shift had already ended. Both sounded certain that the station could solve the problem if the right name appeared. Anton recognized the first caller and offered an answer before Lev had finished the second conversation. Irina could see the relief it would bring: one receiver down, one grateful voice and a friend spared another explanation. Daria asked which promise would remain when Anton went home. The person on the weak line had begun apologizing for taking so long. Lev could hear the apology more clearly than the request.

options.label: Keep both requests open until we know more.
options.reply: Lev leaves two incomplete notes for the next shift, and Anton accepts that a quick offer is not the same thing as an answer.

options.label: Let Anton carry the request privately.
options.reply: His offer frees Lev to hear the other line, while a private promise takes responsibility that the board cannot show.

callback.text: Irina looks at the line carrying her name. She had wanted a question others could see; now she has to leave one visible when it makes the room look less capable.

condition_variants.trigger: has_capitulated = no has_war = no ac_sq_air_capable = yes
condition_variants.text: Irina was returning through a grey afternoon when Lev's second telephone began to ring. The first carried her approach instructions. The other reported that the road used by the incoming maintenance shift had become impassable. Anton held his place beside her and offered to carry the message after landing; Lev had already missed half a sentence trying to answer both people. Irina asked him to finish the approach before he changed receivers. On the ground, Daria discovered that nobody had told the next controller why the second call remained unanswered. The private favor would be quicker. Leaving the problem on the shared board would expose the delay and give somebody else a chance to arrange transport. Irina could still hear the pause in Lev's voice. It had sounded like hesitation until she knew what he was holding.

chapters.title: The Label in Daria's Pocket
chapters.text: Daria turned the suspect connector under a lamp while the apprentice searched his pockets for its label. It belonged to a training rig, but the same checking habit would be used beside an aircraft. One contact had passed a hurried inspection and failed when she flexed the cable. Irina watched Anton arrange the useful tools before anybody asked him to. They could correct the label and inspect the connection now; the question was whether the next shift would learn why it had passed. Daria had signed the original check and could not place the whole error on the apprentice. A shared correction would preserve that responsibility. A quiet repair would get the room working sooner. Outside, someone tested a starter and then shut it down. Nobody at the bench mistook the noise for permission to hurry.

options.label: Keep our names with the correction.
options.reply: The apprentice explains what changed with Irina beside him, losing his anonymity without being left alone to defend the work.

options.label: Let Daria explain it as her own correction.
options.reply: She protects a nervous learner and the crew's immediate confidence, while another useful lesson becomes inseparable from her presence.

callback.text: The earlier account named what made the exercise succeed instead of letting a clean qualification stand for the whole story. Irina asks whether a nervous learner deserves less visible care than someone who finished.

chapters.title: The Visit Anton Promised
chapters.text: Anton had described the family visit as if it were a small errand that could fit between two rehearsals. Lev noticed that he had packed a different shirt, and Daria noticed that the return journey would occupy the hours already written beside his name. Anton offered to rehearse later, then earlier, then with no break at all. Irina recognized the generosity and the hope that nobody would ask which promise mattered more. She wanted another session herself. The board made every missing hour look like a failure to arrange people efficiently. Daria turned it toward the wall for a moment so Anton could speak without measuring his answer against the empty squares.

options.label: Make the visit a visible limit on our plan.
options.reply: Anton can leave without owing an impossible night of work, while Irina must explain why the rehearsal will be shorter.

options.label: Cover the visit quietly among ourselves.
options.reply: The four trade hours to protect his privacy, and Anton begins planning how to repay them before he has left.

callback.text: Anton is still remembered as the person who could make time. Irina wonders whether another private arrangement will teach anyone when to stop asking.

chapters.title: A Better Rehearsal
chapters.text: Anton beat Irina through the desk exercise and immediately explained that her version had contained the harder question. She disliked the consolation more than losing. Lev offered them the same version next time, making the comparison clear enough that neither could hide inside generosity. Daria had heard this conversation often enough to set down two cups before they began. Irina wanted another attempt. Anton wanted her to ask without implying that his first success had been a kindness. The room was safe enough for a small rivalry, provided they could admit that it was one. Otherwise they would spend another evening offering each other turns neither quite believed the other wanted.

options.label: Admit that I want to beat him.
options.reply: Anton laughs with relief; Lev can arrange a fair exercise without pretending it is a favor between selfless colleagues.

options.label: Practice the difficult parts together first.
options.reply: They protect one another from another public comparison, deepening a private partnership whose rules Lev still has to guess.

callback.text: Their first circle made it easy to belong. Irina now notices how much work it takes to disagree without sounding as though she wants to step outside it.

condition_variants.trigger: has_capitulated = no has_war = no ac_sq_air_capable = yes
condition_variants.text: Anton kept describing the training return as if Irina had been given the more difficult exercise. She remembered the same wind and disliked the kindness more than the comparison. Lev had heard them both, and offered an identical desk rehearsal before they argued about the next flying opportunity. Daria brought two cups to the debrief table and asked them to leave the passage clear for the crew outside. Nothing here needed to become a battle story. Irina wanted another turn, Anton wanted his successful correction to count, and both wanted a friendship in which saying so would not sound like ingratitude. The next name on the rehearsal board could settle the practical order without settling the conversation.

chapters.title: The Call Lev Forgot
chapters.text: The caller remembered Lev's voice. Lev did not remember promising to return the call, although the notation in his own notebook left little room to deny it. He had been interrupted, helped someone nearby and let a weak request become the responsibility of a later hour. Anton found the old address and offered to carry a message himself. Daria could repair the immediate mistake without another person learning who had made it. Irina watched Lev turn the notebook so nobody could read over his shoulder. He wanted the caller helped. He also wanted to remain the person the room trusted to remember the voices everyone else missed.

options.label: Let Lev acknowledge the missed promise himself.
options.reply: The caller hears an apology rather than an excuse, and Lev must remain at the receiver long enough to hear the answer.

options.label: Help Anton repair the request quietly.
options.reply: They get the message moving without exposing Lev, while his notebook keeps a private mistake the next shift cannot learn from.

callback.text: The two open notes once let another shift pick up unfinished work. Lev recognizes the difference between leaving a question visible and simply hoping someone else will find it.

chapters.title: The Sound after the Headset
chapters.text: The feedback had stopped, but Anton still heard a thin tone after he took off the training headset. He joked that Lev had finally found a way to keep talking after everyone went home. Daria did not laugh. Irina accompanied him to the clinic, where he answered questions carefully and asked what would happen to the next exercise. The clinician wanted rest from the source of the strain and another review, not a brave demonstration that he could endure it. Anton could accept a formal medical restriction or ask the crew to arrange quiet ground work while he was assessed. Both would help today. Only one would make the limit visible when his willingness became convenient again.

options.label: Record the restriction and protect the review.
options.reply: Anton accepts the difficult public limit; Irina stays with him when people begin asking when he will be back to normal.

options.label: Arrange quiet ground work within the crew.
options.reply: Lev makes room beside the receiver and Daria keeps the immediate strain away, trusting friends to defend a limit others cannot see.

callback.text: The family visit once proved that a visible absence could be allowed to exist. Irina asks Anton whether being useful now should require him to hide why the work has changed.

chapters.title: The Line above the Signature
chapters.text: The account was accurate as far as Irina could check it. The sentence above her signature made that sound like a larger promise. Daria had already marked two qualifications in pencil, and Anton suggested discussing them privately before sending an unnecessarily worrying version onward. Lev read the sentence aloud until the reassuring rhythm stopped sounding like evidence. Irina could sign only the part she knew, forcing the reader to notice the boundary, or trust Daria's private review and keep a clear account for people outside the room. Nobody was asking her to invent a machine or a result. They were asking how much uncertainty a familiar name could carry without being seen.

options.label: Bound my signature to what I actually checked.
options.reply: The account loses its easy conclusion; Daria leaves her qualifications beside Irina's name instead of carrying them privately.

options.label: Let Daria's private check support the account.
options.reply: The familiar name gives readers a useful starting point, while Daria inherits another responsibility that the page cannot explain.

callback.text: Irina remembers standing beside the apprentice whose correction became visible. A signature means less if its owner will share embarrassment only when somebody younger has made the mistake.

chapters.title: A Method without a Miracle
chapters.text: Lev brought a packet to the classroom and Anton searched it for the exciting part. There were measurements, comparison methods and careful explanations of what a result could not prove. Daria said that last section was the exciting part. Irina had been asked to introduce the material to a learner who expected something more decisive than another way of asking a question. The four arranged a demonstration on the table with no machine waiting on their answer. Lev wanted the learner hopeful. Daria wanted her able to repeat the method after the visitors left. Irina could make a modest tool sound useful, or make it sound larger and promise to explain the limits afterward.

options.label: Make the limits part of the first lesson.
options.reply: The learner asks Lev to repeat an uncertain measurement, and the demonstration becomes slower but easier to trust.

options.label: Start with the reassuring account.
options.reply: Anton helps the learner feel welcome, while Daria keeps a separate page ready for the questions the first account has postponed.

callback.text: Lev once had to answer for a promise he forgot. He asks Irina not to let the next lesson depend on remembering to add the difficult part later.

condition_variants.trigger: has_capitulated = no has_global_flag = ac_sp_arkbird_complete YUK = { country_exists = YUK has_country_flag = ac_yuk_arkbird_partner }
condition_variants.text: The completed Arkbird cooperation record had supplied a scientific method, not a promise that a platform would always be there. Lev kept that distinction on the first page. Anton wanted the learner to understand why the modest packet mattered; Daria wanted her able to repeat a measurement without borrowing confidence from an impressive name. Irina arranged the demonstration on the table, where everyone could see the uncertain part instead of imagining it away. She could introduce the limitation with the useful method, or let Anton make a reassuring beginning and save the difficult qualification for later. The learner waited with a pencil, ready to remember whichever version the four taught first.

chapters.title: An Appointment Kept
chapters.text: Anton had an appointment he wanted to postpone. He called it an awkward hour between two useful tasks, which told Irina that the tasks were easier for him to describe than the appointment. Lev offered to accompany him. Daria asked whether he wanted company or merely somebody else to make the decision. The board had acquired a comfortable place for Anton's help. A review might confirm that arrangement, change it or ask him to explain what he had stopped saying aloud. Irina could protect the appointment in the shared plan, leaving its purpose for Anton to disclose, or move the day's work privately until nobody outside the crew noticed an absence.

options.label: Keep the appointment visible and its purpose his.
options.reply: Anton can accept company without making a public confession, and the rest of the station must work around an honest absence.

options.label: Arrange his time privately among the four.
options.reply: He thanks them for avoiding another explanation, while Daria makes room for a limit that still depends on personal memory.

callback.text: The hearing review is not a test of Anton's courage. Irina remembers the thin tone after the headset and asks what he wants the next clinician to know, rather than when he will return to the old work.

chapters.title: The Weak Line Answers
chapters.text: Lev thought the call had ended when the weak voice answered his last question. Anton reached for the next sheet, and Irina almost followed him. Then Daria raised a hand. The voice had answered a different question, one they had stopped asking several minutes earlier. Nobody had lied. A tired operator and an impatient room had simply reached different parts of the conversation. Lev could reopen the exchange and expose the misunderstanding, or let Anton speak privately with the operator while the room continued. Irina looked at the empty chair beside the receiver. It was easy to demand patience from a person who had nowhere to put down the work already waiting.

options.label: Reopen the question where everyone can hear it.
options.reply: The delay becomes visible and Lev must admit what he misheard, giving the next shift a chance to recognize the same mistake.

options.label: Give Anton time with the operator privately.
options.reply: The operator gains a patient listener without an audience, while the shared record keeps the first answer's reassuring shape.

callback.text: The crew once repaired Lev's missed call quietly. Irina cannot tell whether that kindness taught him to ask for help sooner or taught the rest of them how much could disappear from an account.

condition_variants.trigger: has_capitulated = no has_war = no ac_sq_air_capable = yes
condition_variants.text: The weak reply arrived while Irina was trying to establish a clear approach. It answered a question Lev had abandoned several minutes earlier. She almost treated the familiar words as a new clearance. Anton, working on the ground beside the receiver, asked which question had actually been answered. Lev started the exchange again and Irina held until she understood it. After landing, Daria drew two separate lines on the board: what the pilot had heard and what the controller had intended. Neither line accused anyone of lying. Anton offered to speak privately with the tired operator while the next task continued. Irina could accept that kindness or reopen the misunderstanding with the whole shift. The aircraft was back. The next crew still needed an answer that belonged to the question they were asking.

chapters.title: Yesterday's Date
chapters.text: The component had been checked, but the board gave yesterday's date and the person who remembered doing it had gone off shift. Daria found an intermittent connection that disappeared whenever she held the cable still. Anton fetched a lamp with his back to the receiver, sparing his ears the continuing hiss. Irina could ask him to find the earlier checker privately, or stop the shared handover while Daria established what the entry meant. Lev wanted the person who had written the date to speak before the mistake became a rumor. Neither option made a damaged connection safe by itself; Daria kept it on the bench. The decision was whether the correction would travel with the work or depend on the four remembering whom they had told. Anton rested the lamp where a new apprentice could hold it.

options.label: Ask for a shared correction without inventing a motive.
options.reply: Daria leaves the missing explanation visible, and Lev gives the clerk time to answer before anyone writes a story about blame.

options.label: Let Daria settle the condition and speak privately.
options.reply: The immediate work becomes reliable without a public dispute, but its history remains dependent on a conversation others did not hear.

callback.text: Irina once limited what her signature could mean. The old choice makes it harder to mistake today's useful check for proof that yesterday's account was already sound.

chapters.title: The Empty Hook
chapters.text: Anton took his gloves off the hook and put them in a drawer. Irina felt an absurd urge to stop him, as if the hook were a promise the room had made. He said he was tired of visitors learning his old job before they asked what he did now. Lev had arranged a place at the teaching table. Daria had left practical work there, not a ceremonial task to keep him occupied. Anton could explain the change himself, allowing strangers to ask clumsy questions, or the crew could protect him with a concise introduction and let him choose when the longer account became public. The empty hook would remain either way.

options.label: Let Anton introduce the work he does now.
options.reply: He answers one awkward question without being rescued, and Irina learns to offer respect without promising his old place back.

options.label: Give him a protected introduction first.
options.reply: Lev keeps the room comfortable while Anton begins the lesson, leaving the more difficult account within the people who already know him.

callback.text: The quiet reassignment helped after the headset strain. Anton says that being protected then should not mean everybody else gets to decide how his work is described forever.

chapters.title: The Envelope beside the Receiver
chapters.text: Lev left the envelope closed until Irina sat down. It contained an account whose neat cover invited a more confident answer than the notes inside supported. Anton set a second chair beside the receiver so nobody would have to explain the uncertainty standing alone. Daria asked who would sign the question if the answer failed to arrive. They were not deciding a country's policy in the small room. They were deciding how a personal voice would survive being passed onward by people with more authority and less time. Irina could leave the qualification on the shared cover, or call the next recipient privately and trust them to carry it without the paper's help.

options.label: Put the qualification beside the shared account.
options.reply: Lev sends a question another shift can still recognize, while Anton accepts that the room may be asked to defend its hesitation.

options.label: Call the recipient before sending it onward.
options.reply: The private call gives a real person room to listen, but Daria cannot show the next learner which promise now holds the account together.

callback.text: The learner once repeated the uncertain measurement instead of treating a method as a miracle. Irina wants the next recipient to inherit the same permission to ask again.

chapters.title: Who Will Answer the Next Voice
chapters.text: The next operator arrived before the four had agreed how to describe the difficult exchange. Irina had written what she remembered, Lev had marked the words he could not confirm and Daria had made tea nobody touched. Anton offered to take the questions. He was good at making another person's embarrassment feel survivable; he was less good at refusing to carry all of it himself. The newcomer needed an account that would remain useful after the familiar faces left. Irina could ask the four to share their uncertainty openly, or keep a protected debrief and give the next shift only the part they could stand behind together. Both meant leaving something unfinished.

options.label: Share the uncertainty with the incoming operator.
options.reply: Lev leaves the unanswered words visible; Anton stays to help Irina answer rather than becoming the person who answers for everyone.

options.label: Protect the debrief within the four.
options.reply: Daria gives tired people room to speak without an audience, while the newcomer receives a bounded account with a quieter history.

callback.text: The qualification on the envelope survives on the incoming operator's page. Irina has to decide whether the personal account deserves the same visible uncertainty.

chapters.capitulated_text: Lev balanced the receiver on a borrowed table while Daria found four chairs. The country's capitulation had changed the work the station could perform, but it had not explained the uncertain exchange waiting in Irina's folder. Anton offered to take the first questions from the incoming operator. Irina knew the kindness and the danger of letting him carry every difficult answer. They could preserve their uncertainty where others would have to see it, or protect the exhausted debrief and pass onward a narrower account. Neither would restore a state or prove a national outcome. Daria poured the tea before it went cold, leaving a small ordinary task inside a room whose larger promises had changed.

condition_variants.text: Other participants had entered the fighting. Lev crossed out a heading that made two countries sound like the whole conflict and left room for what the room could not know. Irina's own exchange was difficult enough to explain. Anton offered to answer the next operator's questions, and Daria asked whether he meant to help or to make everybody else's embarrassment disappear. They could share the uncertainty openly or keep the debrief protected and give the incoming shift a bounded account. Neither choice authorized them to promise peace, judge a winner or decide what distant allies intended. The new operator needed a useful place to begin, not a confident ending the four could not establish.

condition_variants.trigger: has_capitulated = no has_war = no has_global_flag = ac_cpw_declaration_withheld
condition_variants.text: The country's mandate had withheld its declaration. Anton repeated the wording carefully: a national decision, not evidence that the other side had agreed to everything. Lev placed the incoming shift's folder beside an exchange whose missing words still needed to remain missing. Irina felt relief and the urge to let it improve the account. Daria asked her to wait until the tea was poured before answering anyone. They could preserve the uncertainty openly or protect the four people's debrief and send only what they could defend. An avoided declaration had not made an uncertain voice certain. The new operator would need a method that remained useful after relief stopped being the strongest feeling in the room.

condition_variants.trigger: has_capitulated = no has_war = no has_global_flag = ac_cpw_prevented
condition_variants.text: The reciprocal exchange had closed this declaration route. Lev wrote that much and stopped before adding a promise about every future voice. Irina could understand the wish for a complete ending, particularly while Anton smiled at news that let the room breathe more easily. Daria brought the next shift's folder back to the center of the table. A difficult exchange remained to be described, including words none of them could confirm. Irina could share the uncertainty with the new operator or protect the personal debrief and send a narrower account. They were allowed to be relieved. They were still responsible for deciding which parts of that relief belonged in another person's instructions.

condition_variants.text: A flash beyond the cloud made Irina begin a turn before Lev completed the warning. The next instruction broke under static. Anton, listening from the ground, asked Lev to repeat the direction rather than supply the part he could not hear. Irina held the changed heading until she understood where she was being sent; the other aircraft became a pale shape beyond her wing and then disappeared into weather again. At the debrief Daria asked which observations would help the next crew survive the same uncertainty. Anton sat beside the receiver, with no suggestion that his useful question had restored his old flying role. The war between the two countries was real. Its existence did not identify every light or voice. Irina could preserve the uncertain exchange openly or protect the exhausted conversation within the four. Lev left room beneath the words he had actually received.

chapters.title: The Person before the Voice
chapters.text: Anton asked the new operators to introduce themselves before putting on the classroom headsets. One expected a trick and gave a call number. Anton waited until Lev supplied his own name first. The lesson was not about remembering everyone perfectly. It was about noticing that a weak reply came from a person whose hesitation might have a reason beyond incompetence. Irina listened from the back while Daria watched an apprentice adjust a chair without being asked. Anton could use his own experience to make the lesson concrete, or teach the method while keeping the experience private. Irina would need to support either choice without turning gratitude into a demand for disclosure.

options.label: Let Anton decide how much of himself to teach.
options.reply: The lesson pauses long enough for his consent to matter, and the learners see that respect is more than a sympathetic story.

options.label: Keep his experience private and teach the method.
options.reply: Irina gives the class a usable exercise without asking Anton to become its example, while the deeper lesson remains less visible.

callback.text: Irina remembers the medical restriction after the feedback injury. The knowledge makes her careful, not entitled: Anton can choose which parts of that experience strangers are allowed to hear.

chapters.title: The Instructor's Spare Pencil
chapters.text: Lev's old radio instructor died after a long illness. The family sent a small packet containing a spare pencil and a note explaining that he had always carried two because a learner would forget one. Lev held it as though it were difficult equipment. Anton remembered a man impatient with elegant answers and unexpectedly patient with frightened people. Daria asked whether the family wanted anything returned. Irina thought the next class might welcome the story, then noticed Lev had not yet spoken about it even to them. A death outside the crew had left a place inside it. They could ask permission to share the memory, or allow the pencil to remain a private thing rather than make every loss teach somebody a lesson.

options.label: Ask before putting his memory into a lesson.
options.reply: Lev writes to the family in his own words, accepting that a moving account still belongs partly to people outside the room.

options.label: Keep the pencil and the memory among friends.
options.reply: The four make room for Lev's silence, protecting a private grief without trying to turn its meaning into useful work.

callback.text: They once protected an appointment without owning its purpose. Irina offers Lev the same ordinary space now, without asking when he will be ready to explain.

chapters.title: Room for Another Name
chapters.text: The new apprentice could not find a place for her name. The board still carried the four familiar ones beside tasks now taught by other people. Irina had stopped noticing how much authority the old handwriting claimed. Daria offered a clean cloth, and Anton objected that erasing a line did not have to mean forgetting who had done the work. Lev drew a fresh column. They could leave a visible history with the new names, showing where responsibility had changed hands, or keep the familiar board and arrange the apprentice's place privately until she felt ready. Irina looked at her first small line in the corner. Someone had once made room without knowing what she would become.

options.label: Show the handover and give her a real line.
options.reply: The apprentice gains responsibility she can explain without borrowing an old name, and the four must accept that she will answer differently.

options.label: Let her begin within the familiar arrangement.
options.reply: Daria gives her quiet practical support, preserving continuity while the board still makes the old crew look more necessary than they are.

callback.text: The spare pencil sits beside the cloth. Lev says that keeping a memory should leave someone else room to begin, not make a person who has gone impossible to replace.

chapters.title: The Board They Leave
chapters.text: The board was ready before the room was. A new learner had written a question beside a component and left enough space for the answer to change. Daria approved the spacing, which made Anton laugh until she asked him to improve it. Lev put the spare receiver where someone could reach it from the extra chair. Irina had imagined a final explanation that would make all their choices fit together. Instead the learner wanted to know who she should ask when the written method stopped helping. They could leave the names of people willing to answer and a history of questions that had remained open, or a clear signed account that kept the difficult personal history within the four.

options.label: Leave the unfinished questions with the new names.
options.reply: The learner inherits permission to disagree as well as a method, and the four leave work that no longer needs their constant presence.

options.label: Sign the account we can all defend.
options.reply: They give the learner a stable first method while keeping the most difficult explanations among the friends who made them possible.

callback.text: The new line already contains a question Irina would have phrased differently. She leaves the pencil beside it instead of correcting the learner's voice into her own.

endings.title: Names beside the Questions
endings.text: Daria wipes an old mark from the board and leaves the correction visible. The learner asks why it changed. Nobody tells her that knowing the method should have made the question unnecessary. Anton brings another chair into the circle; Lev repeats the uncertain part without changing it into a confident instruction. Irina sees her first name in the corner, small enough now that other names can fit beside it. The four have not made every promise safe or every account complete. They have learned to leave a place where another person can answer without first pretending to know more than they do. Their friendship includes mistakes someone was allowed to name, limits someone was allowed to keep and grief that did not have to justify itself as a lesson. When the learner takes the pencil, all four remain present long enough to hear her own first explanation.

endings.title: The Account They Can Defend
endings.text: The board is neat and the signed account is useful. Daria has tested what it says, Lev has made the instructions clear and Anton knows how to help the first nervous learner through them. Irina can defend every printed sentence. The difficult conversations are kept elsewhere, among people who remember why a harmless phrase once made somebody look away. That privacy has protected real friendships. It has also left the next crew dependent on names whose history it cannot see. A learner asks whether an exception belongs on the board. Irina answers carefully and notices how much rests on being in the room to answer. The four do not leave in anger. They leave competent work, a protected account and affection that remains strongest inside its familiar circle. The next people will have to decide for themselves which questions can be asked beyond it.

endings.title: The Clips Left Empty
endings.text: The clips make small sounds as the four remove their papers. All four are alive to take their work elsewhere, and there is no single betrayal large enough to put in a final account. Anton has work he can teach elsewhere. Daria carries a notebook of checks she will make useful to another set of hands. Lev carefully labels the receiver's awkward switch before handing it over. Irina signs what they can still agree on and leaves space beneath it. They have been kind in ways that did not always let the others speak, and honest in ways that did not always let them remain close. The next learner will inherit real skills and a board whose empty places have more than one explanation. Outside, Anton waits until the other three have their belongings. Their goodbyes are ordinary, which makes them harder. Then the familiar voices take different routes home.
